name: MOON
summary: MOON is a historical molybdenum-100 double-beta and solar-neutrino detector concept. Its MOON-1 prototype tested a layered scintillator approach; it did not realize the proposed tonne-scale physics experiment.
detection_principle: Thin double-beta source foils alternate with plastic scintillator plates. Coincident electrons provide energy and topology information; optical collection determines resolution and rejection of two-neutrino-decay backgrounds.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: MOON-1 measured scintillator response with calibration electrons. The reported 6.8% FWHM resolution near 3 MeV is prototype performance, not a neutrinoless-decay sensitivity achieved with a tonne of isotope.

results.summary: MOON-1 measured scintillator response with calibration electrons. The reported 6.8% FWHM resolution near 3 MeV is prototype performance, not a neutrinoless-decay sensitivity achieved with a tonne of isotope.

science_scope: A neutrinoless decay would violate lepton number. Half-life sensitivity is a forecast unless explicitly reported as an experimental limit; its interpretation as an effective Majorana mass depends on the decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements.
